about: Every display name of the game: one entry for each internal key. `tongue` is plain (English), hearth (the householders' tongue), sand (the sand-country tongue) or cutters (Sanskrit proper). `from` lists the roots of a name in a tongue, as lang/derive.mjs reads them. `other` holds what other peoples call the same thing. `shown: false` marks a name that is for the glossary and for writers and is not shown in play. `same` points to the entry that names the same thing. Run `node lang/derive.mjs --check names.json` after any change, and `node lang/glossary.mjs` to write glossary.md again.

generated.rule: A tool or a piece of armour has no name of its own in the source. Its name is the tier word, a space, and the piece word. Tools exist at all ten tiers and armour from iron up. Swords, bows, staves and totems are written out in the source and have entries of their own in names, made by the same rule with Sword, Bow, Staff and Totem.
generated.prompt: Needs a <tier word> pick or better. The article is an before Iron, Antar and Ākās.

names.name: Peopls Craft
names.why: The name of the players and of what they do: the born's word for those who come up at the mouth, and the work the born cannot do and live (1.5). It stays as it is.

names.name: Agility
names.why: The game's measure of practice (1.6). The plain word stays.

names.name: Arm
names.why: The blue bar measures the arm: how much more it will take before it stops answering (1.6, 6.6). Practice at driving hardens it. Arcana claimed stored power and spells (8.11).

names.name: Strength
names.why: A person gets better at what they do, and attribute points are the game's measure of that (1.6). The plain word stays.

names.name: Vitality
names.meaning: how much a body will take
names.why: The game's measure of practice (1.6). The plain word stays.

names.name: Empty Hands
names.meaning: the first steps of the order of work
names.why: An arrival comes up at the mouth with empty hands, and the first steps are the cutter's own trade (1.6). First light is the hour a holder lifts the hand, and no step of the Guide wins it (8.11).

names.name: Iron and Root
names.meaning: iron, and the first of the eight
names.why: Nothing false: the chapter takes a crew from iron to the animal bodied in root (4.3). It stays.

names.name: The Deep Stone
names.meaning: the deep rock of the living ground
names.why: Nothing false. It stays.

names.name: Under the World
names.why: Arrivals speak of under the world and above it (3.1). It stays.

names.name: Above the World
names.why: Arrivals speak of under the world and above it, and above carries their false belief about the islands (1.8, 3.1). It stays as an arrival's word.

names.name: The Dark Night
names.meaning: the night the moon is dark
names.why: The ground chapter's plain words for the eighth night of the moon's round (1.6). The old title, with the first, made light a thing won by killing (8.11).

names.name: After the Last
names.meaning: what follows the last of the eight
names.why: The ground chapter's own heading for what a crew can do once the eighth is dead (1.6). Nothing ends there, so the word for an ending goes.

names.name: Guide
names.why: The Guide is the order of work as the householders tell it (1.6 The Guide). The present name is already right and stays.

names.name: Crystal-work
names.why: A staff is crystal on cut lines, and driving it is the same act as holding a ward, pointed at a body (5.7, 6.6). The chapters call the craft crystal-work. Magic claimed spells (8.11).

names.name: Melee
names.why: Standing between the animals and the hand on the stone (5.7, 8.4). The plain word stays.

names.name: Ranged
names.why: The bow is how a held place kills from inside what it has turned back and what flies over (5.7, 8.4). The plain word stays.

names.name: Totem
names.why: A totem carries food, and a small feeder forms on it and stays for the food (5.7, 6.6). Nothing is summoned or bound, so the label is the thing that is carried.

names.name: The Living Ground
names.meaning: the ground of a living world, as against the two remains of the earlier world
names.why: Nobody named it. Arrivals know the frame and tell the ground of a living world from the remains of a dead one, and the hollow and the islands are remains (1.3). It is the ground chapter's own plain word.

other.name: the ground
other.meaning: the householders' plain word. They hold that it is the only ground there is (1.8)

names.name: The Hollow
names.why: The ground chapter's plain word for the inside of the root, which has the wood for floor and for roof (1.3, 3.4). Arrivals who cross say the hollow, and the gate that leads there is the Hollow Gate. The old name glued two nouns and was also the name of a country inside the place.

other.name: Under
other.meaning: the householders' word. They say what comes up at night comes from it, and none of them has seen it (3.6)

other.name: Koṭara
other.meaning: the hollow of a tree: the cutting trade's word for a hollow inside wood. It is for the glossary only, because the plain word is true of the place (L.11)

names.name: The Islands
names.meaning: the islands left of the earlier world
names.why: The ground chapter's plain word for what is left of the world that grew on the root: islands in two layers with nothing under them (1.3, 3.5). The gate that leads there is the Island Gate. The old name glued two nouns and stated the arrivals' false belief as fact. Householders have no word for the place at all (3.6).

other.name: above the world
other.meaning: what arrivals say of it. They hold that the islands are in the sky over the living ground, which is false (1.8, 3.1)

names.name: Vela
names.why: The born name the low edge of the land, where they make the salt every charge is packed in, by their word for a shore that is also a limit (3.2 beach).

names.name: Kusum
names.why: A rare country of short pale turf and thick flowers. The born name it for the flowers and cannot say why they grow there (3.2 bloomvale).

names.name: Pabbat
names.why: The born name the high stone country, where hard rock lies at the surface and the first comers cut their housing stone, by their word for a mountain (3.2 crags).

names.name: Marudesha
names.why: The sand-country people's name for their own country, the dry waste where the burrower let nothing else come up (3.2 desert, 5.3). The same word is in their name for the burrower.

other.name: Marudes
other.meaning: the householders' form of the same two words

names.name: Vana
names.why: The born call the old oak wood, where villages stand whole under the trees, simply the wood; the pale wood is named against it (3.2 forest).

names.name: Fungus Caverns
names.why: Named in plain words by the arrivals who cross by gate, for what they find: caverns floored with turf and great capped fungi on everything that has died there; no born person has seen it (3.4 hollows, 3.6).

names.name: Crystal Caverns
names.why: Named in plain words by arrivals for its bare floors and spires of azure and violet crystal; the same kind of place as the crystal caverns of the deep rock, and the bible calls those so (3.3, 3.4 hollows_crystal).

names.name: Aranna
names.why: The born name the hot wet wood by their word for wild forest away from any settlement, because no flock lives in it and no village was ever built there (3.2 jungle).

names.name: Samudda
names.why: The born name the one water by their word for the sea: all open water lies at one height and nothing comes up in it (3.1, 3.2 ocean).

names.name: Davalavan
names.why: The born read how long a country has been left from its trees, open grass, then pale wood, then oak, and name the light wood of pale-barked trees on lately given-up pasture for its white bark (3.2 palewood).

names.name: Sānu
names.meaning: a summit, ridge, the top of a mountain
names.why: The ground above the snow, where nothing grows. The born name it for what it is, the tops of the high country (3.2 peaks).

names.name: Yavas
names.why: The born name the open grass for what it is to a hearth, which is pasture. The first comers cleared it for flocks, and the flocks have gone wild and still graze it (3.2 plains).

names.name: Island Meadow
names.why: Named in plain words by arrivals for the turf, grass, flowers and lit-leaved trees of the earlier world's surface, where the first comers camped (3.5 rift).

names.name: Crystal Islands
names.why: Named in plain words by arrivals for the islands set with spires of pale crystal, the pasture of the island kinds (3.5 rift_shards).

names.name: Kāsa
names.meaning: kāśa, a tall grass used for mats and roofs
names.why: The born, who have villages here, name the country for the tall dry grass that covers it between trees cut thin for fuel (3.2 savanna).

other.name: Darudesha
other.meaning: timber country: the nearest wood to the sand, cut for the fires for as long as fires have burned there (3.2 savanna)

names.name: Panka
names.why: Wet lowland that never drains, where nobody built. The born name it for the mud (3.2 swamp).

names.name: Tusāravan
names.why: The born name the cold pine wood by its cold, the cause of what they know of it: snow on its higher ground and none of the day kinds of feeder (3.2 taiga).

names.name: Hima
names.why: Flat and white, with snow on the grass. No village was ever raised in it, and the born name it for the snow they see lying on it (3.2 tundra).

names.name: Vault
names.why: Plain word: one room of dressed stone in the hollow, open at its doorway, as the bible calls it (3.7 cache1).

names.name: Island Store
names.why: A small store of the first comers hung between the two layers of the islands, sealed by air because an island has no depth of rock to cut a room under (3.7). It has no name in play today.

names.name: Sealed Store
names.why: Plain words for what it is: a crews' store of dressed stone cut under solid rock with no way in from above, sealed and full (3.7 dungeon, 2.3).

names.name: Broken Store
names.meaning: a store that has been broken into
names.why: Plain words for what it is: a small surface store of the born hunters, its walls broken out by feeders, sand-country people and householders short of lees; nothing on this ground falls into ruin by itself (3.1, 3.7 ruin, 2.4).

names.name: Village
names.why: Nobody needs another word: four to six houses round a well, whole and empty, which householders on the road still use (3.7 village).

names.name: Peopls
names.meaning: persons with a sound left out; ones who look like persons and do not die when killed
names.why: Already right: the born's word for arrivals, written peopls in the game's English in every mouth, and taken by arrivals for themselves (1.5, 5.6, L.9).

other.name: Manuss
other.meaning: Manussa, a person, with its last sound left out on purpose. Made by hand, and never shown (L.9)

other.name: Manūsh
other.meaning: Manūsha, a person, with its last sound left out on purpose. Made by hand, and never shown (L.9)

other.name: crew, cutter
other.meaning: what arrivals also say among themselves, words of the trade they came with (5.6)

names.name: Householders
names.why: The ground chapter's plain word for the born who hold hearths (1.4, 5.2).

other.name: Gahapat
other.meaning: the master of a house: what one of them is called in their own tongue. For the glossary only

names.name: sand-country people
names.meaning: the people of the sand country
names.why: The plain words of the ground chapter for the born who burn what they kill (1.4, 5.3). Game text says them in English. Ashen was a word for a faction and had no cause.

other.name: Maruzana
other.meaning: people of the waste: what they call themselves, after the country the burrower held (5.3)

other.name: Marujan
other.meaning: the householders' form of the same two words

names.name: Vanahar
names.meaning: holding the wood (vana, a forest, wood + dhara, holding, bearing; dh between vowels wears to h)
names.why: Householders say each great feeder was set over its country by the forebears and can be seen to hold it, as a lit stone did (4.11, 5.2). This one lies at the stones of the woodland kinds, in the country they call Vana, a short walk from the mouth (4.3).

other.name: the woodland strongest
other.meaning: what arrivals call it: the strongest of the woodland host, the first of the order of work (4.11)

names.name: Kuranga
names.why: It runs on four legs and carries tines, which is the shape of the deep kind's largest (4.9). The born say that on the dark night the moon is hollow and what was in it has come down, and they name the largest of what came down for the animal it looks like (1.6, 1.8).

other.name: the deep strongest
other.meaning: what arrivals call it: the strongest of the deep kind (4.9)

names.name: Ratan
names.why: No born person has seen it, and householders have no word for the islands (3.6). What they have is the pattern of its bait, which is a lens, and the telling that the animal is bodied in crystal and that light calls it (4.8). They name it for a gem.

other.name: the crystal strongest
other.meaning: what arrivals call it: the strongest of the islands' crystal kinds (4.8)

names.name: Maruhar
names.meaning: holding the waste (maru, a sandy waste, desert + dhara, holding)
names.why: Householders give the burrower the name of a thing that holds a country, as they do the woodland one, for the waste that is its own ground (4.4, 4.11, 5.2).

other.name: Marudara
other.meaning: holding the waste: the same two words worn the sand country's way. The sand-country people held the burrower above themselves as the thing that held their country (5.3)

other.name: the burrower
other.meaning: what arrivals call it (4.4)

names.name: Jīmūt
names.why: Storm is the born's word for the animal overhead (4.7). It is pale, it never lands, and what it throws falls from above, so they name it as they name a cloud. The old name made it a regent.

other.name: the flier
other.meaning: what arrivals call it (4.7)

names.name: Nihān
names.meaning: a store, hoard; a place for depositing anything
names.why: Householders say their forebears closed their first and best stone under the cairn to save it for the day it could be lit again, and their telling makes the animal that comes up through the base a store that can be opened (4.10).

other.name: Dūmara
other.meaning: dying hard, tenacious of life. The sand-country people say the heap was closed over a thing that could not be killed, by people who then set lamps round it (4.10)

other.name: the stone-eater
other.meaning: what arrivals call it: the strongest of the stone-eating kind, in the base of the eighth stone (4.10)

names.name: Guhamāt
names.meaning: mother of the caves (guhā, a cave + mātṛ, a mother, any mother, said also of animals)
names.why: The born say mother of it, because small feeders form round the large one on the pieces of cap that fall from it (4.6, 4.13). No householder has seen the hollow (3.6), so the saying is one that came down with the telling of the Guide, and the caves are where the telling puts it.

other.name: the fungus strongest
other.meaning: what arrivals call it: the strongest of the hollow's fungus kinds (4.6)

names.name: Kankāl
names.why: Householders know the shade-kind as the dark thing that comes to anything dead on land, and they sink their own dead in water against it (5.2, 7.3). Its strongest is pale where the rest are dark, and the pillars of its floor are stacked bone (4.5). They name it for bone. The old name made it a warden over a sealed way, and nothing was sealed (4.13).

other.name: the shade strongest
other.meaning: what arrivals call it: the strongest of the shade-kind (4.5)

names.name: Vanagan
names.why: The woodland kinds feed on green growth and fed in the woods while their strongest lived (4.3, 7.3). The born name the kind for the country, as they name its strongest.

other.name: woodland host
other.meaning: the plain words the bible and arrivals use

names.name: Vālukagan
names.why: The sand kinds feed on stone and where they feed in the open it falls to sand; their own ground is the sand country (4.4). The kinds of feeder are named by the born (L.1); the kind has no display name in the game today.

other.name: Maruyūta
other.meaning: pack of the waste: the sand-country word for the host of their own country

other.name: sand host
other.meaning: the plain words the bible and arrivals use

names.name: Tamagan
names.why: The born call the common animal of this kind by their word for darkness, and the kind by the same word (7.3).

other.name: shade-kind
other.meaning: the plain words the bible and arrivals use

names.name: Guhagan
names.why: The fungus kinds of the hollow. The born have the kind only from the telling, and name it for the caves where the telling puts its mother (4.6).

other.name: fungus host
other.meaning: the plain words the bible and arrivals use

names.name: Ākāsagan
names.why: The flying kinds feed on whatever is in the air, and their strongest never lands (4.7, 7.3). The born name the kind for the open air over them.

other.name: flying host
other.meaning: the plain words the bible and arrivals use

names.name: Sakalagan
names.meaning: host of splinters (śakala, a chip, fragment, splinter + -gaṇa)
names.why: The kinds of the islands are bodied in splintered crystal (1.6, 4.8). The kinds of feeder are named by the born (L.1); the kind has no display name in the game today.

other.name: crystal host
other.meaning: the plain words the bible and arrivals use

names.name: Chandagan
names.meaning: host of the moon (candra, the moon + -gaṇa)
names.why: Everyone says the things of the dark night come down from the moon, so the householders' name for the deep kind has the moon in it (1.8, L.2). The kinds of feeder are named by the born (L.1); the kind has no display name in the game today.

other.name: deep kind
other.meaning: the plain words the bible and arrivals use

names.name: Pāsānagan
names.why: The stone-eating kind feeds on rock and coal everywhere under the ground and its strongest is bodied in dressed stone (4.10, 7.3). The kinds of feeder are named by the born (L.1); the kind has no display name in the game today.

other.name: stone-eating kind
other.meaning: the plain words the bible and arrivals use

names.name: Kajjot
names.namer: the first comers, through the born
names.why: It has no lasting shape. It forms round old crystal in the air over the islands, and what is seen is a bright point moving by itself (7.3). The first comers named it for the lit insect, and the name came down through the born (L.1).

names.name: Dāhaga
names.why: His people name him for his work: the long iron with the basket head is the tool they burn a carcass with where it lies, and he throws its burning pitch (7.4, 5.3); Hexer states a spell and goes.

other.name: Dāhak
other.meaning: burning, setting on fire

names.name: Shūra
names.meaning: a strong or valiant man, a warrior
names.why: A fighter with a blade who marches for a fire (5.3, 7.4). The name is what his own people call a man who marches. Ashen was a word for a faction and had no cause.

other.name: Sūra
other.meaning: the householders' form of the same word

names.name: Kaddam
names.why: The born know it only as a head showing in the mud of the mire, where it comes up and lies, and name it for the mud it is bodied in (7.3).

names.name: Boar
names.why: A tusked rooter of the cold woods (7.2) is an ordinary animal arrivals know; the glued Burrow+hog goes for the plain word.

names.name: Lūta
names.why: A small eight-legged crawler bodied in fibre and in the white thread that fungus puts through rock (7.3). The born name it for the animal it looks like.

names.name: Angār
names.why: What is seen is a live coal in the air over the sand and the molten rock, and the born name it for that coal; the sand-country people, whose fires have wisps over them, say their own form of the same word (7.3, 5.3).

other.name: Angāra
other.meaning: the same word as the sand-country people say it. The wisps hang over the warm ash of their fires (7.3)

names.name: Jatu
names.why: Householders see it at night over the crags and peaks, a flier that roosts and hangs under overhangs, and call it a bat (7.3, 7.6).

names.name: Kīta
names.namer: the first comers, through the born
names.why: A plated six-legged crawler shed from between the burrower's plates, named by the first comers who brought the burrower up for what it plainly is, an insect (7.3, 4.4, L.1).

names.name: Hare
names.why: A small long-eared runner of the sand and dry grass that runs and stands still by turns (7.2) is a hare to anyone who has seen one.

names.name: Vaka
names.why: A pale four-legged runner of the cold country that follows at the edge of sight in ones to threes (7.3). The born of the pine villages name it for the animal it looks like. The old name was an adjective and a noun.

names.name: Kinva
names.why: It has no lasting shape and forms in the jelly that rots out of fallen growth (7.3). The born see a lump of that rot moving in the grass and name it for the rot. The old name glued two nouns.

names.name: Fish
names.why: A bright fish in any water, the one creature no feeder shares its country with (7.2, 3.1), is an ordinary fish; the glued Glimmer+fin goes.

names.name: Tama
names.why: The born, who sit up at their hearths beside their dead because of it, see an upright dark thing the height of a person that is the commonest thing in the dark and name it for that (7.3, 5.2).

names.name: Sagāl
names.namer: the first comers, through the born
names.why: A long-jawed runner of the hollow that feeds on the fungus kinds on sufferance (7.3). No born person has seen it. The name is the one the first comers gave it, for the animal it looks like, as it came down through the born (L.1). The old name glued two nouns.

names.name: Grouse
names.why: A knee-high ground bird of woods, grass and wet country that calls all day (7.2) is a bird arrivals know as a grouse; the cute coinage goes.

names.name: Ulūk
names.why: The deep kind's flier, in the air on the dark night only. It calls before it stoops, and the call is heard before anything is seen (7.3). The born name it for the night bird that does the same.

names.name: Jālak
names.why: The trade names it by its look, an ember in the air (7.5, 5.5 beastcaller); Spirit states a wrong belief and goes.

names.name: Dīpik
names.why: What forms on the totem whose head is a lamp from the housing of an eighth stone is a point of yellow light, and the trade names it for the lamp (7.5, 4.10, 5.5 beastcaller); Cairnlight is a glued pair and says the cairn is lit.

names.name: Harinak
names.why: The trade names it by its look, a dark four-legged thing with pale tines a hand high (7.5, 5.5 beastcaller); Moonbound says something binds it to the moon, and nothing does.

names.name: Chattak
names.why: The trade names it by its look, a small lit fungus cap like a little parasol (7.5, 5.5 beastcaller); Sprite states a wrong belief and goes.

names.name: Jatuk
names.why: The trade names it by its look, a small dark flier (7.5, 5.5 beastcaller); Bound says something binds it, and nothing does (7.5).

names.name: Sakalak
names.why: The trade names it by its look, a lit splinter like a small one of the island kind (7.5, 7.3, 5.5 beastcaller).

names.name: Sūlak
names.why: The trade that feeds small feeders by hand names each by its look, and what forms on an iron totem is a green lump with a thorn (7.5, 5.5 beastcaller); its old name was the same as the wild kind's.

names.name: Kanik
names.why: What forms on the totem with a head of the gem is a point of the gem's colour, and the trade names it for a speck (7.5, 5.5 beastcaller). The old name called it a wisp of light.

names.name: Setasalaha
names.why: The trade names it by its look, a small white flier, and calls such a flier a moth as it calls the wild one (7.5, 7.3, 5.5 beastcaller); Zephyr is a wind and says nothing true of it.

names.name: Chandasāvak
names.why: The born say that on the dark night the moon is hollow and what was in it has come down, so their name for the deep kind makes it the moon's young, which is false: it comes up out of the root (1.6, 1.8, L.2).

names.name: Asikavak
names.namer: the first comers, through the born
names.why: The first comers met it in their vaults in the hollow, a fungus two strides tall with one limb grown out into an edge, and the name came down with the trade (7.3, 5.4, L.1); Knight says it is a person and goes.

names.name: Vihanga
names.namer: the first comers, through the born
names.why: The flier of the islands, broad and scaled, which rides under an island rim and never lands (7.3). No born person has seen it. The name is the one the first comers gave it, as it came down through the born (L.1).

names.name: Nihirakka
names.why: The born say it was posted in the sealed stores, so their name is that of a thing set to guard a store, which is false: it nests on its food (7.3); Sentinel states the same belief as a title and goes.

names.name: Sakal
names.namer: the first comers, through the born
names.why: Its shards are the bait for the strongest of the islands, which the born teach in the Guide, and the kind is named for the splintered crystal it is bodied in (7.3, 4.8).

names.name: Bedaga
names.why: The breaker: the biggest of a march, who carries a beam for doors and chests and walks at the nearest door (7.4). His people name him for the work.

other.name: Bedak

names.name: Kavak
names.namer: the first comers, through the born
names.why: Its sacs are the bait for the strongest of the hollow, which the born teach in the Guide, and the name came down from the first comers with the trade for what is seen: a lit cap that hops (7.3, 4.6, L.1).

names.name: Paroha
names.namer: the first comers, through the born
names.why: The least of the woodland host, bodied in sprout, named by kind for what it is bodied in as the first comers knew it at the first stones (7.3, 4.3, L.1); the diminutive goes.

names.name: Silahādak
names.namer: the first comers, through the born
names.why: A plated crawler that feeds on rock, and on coal where it finds it. It is found with its head against a wall or a seam, and its grinding carries through rock (7.3). The first comers met it in their stores and their diggings and named it for what it does, and the name came down through the born.

names.name: Kantak
names.why: The born walk the woods by day past a body of bramble standing rooted among the bushes and taken for one, and name it for what it is bodied in (7.3, 1.6).

names.name: Salaha
names.namer: the first comers, through the born
names.why: Its dust is what the kite bait carries up, which the born teach in the Guide, and they call the flier that leaves it a moth (7.3, 4.7).

names.name: Sheep
names.why: A horned grazer in a heavy coat that runs in small herds is the flocks gone wild that people here live on (1.6, 7.2); arrivals know the animal, so it has the plain word, and the glued Wool+back goes.

names.name: Vejja
names.why: A householder whose trade is the holder's body: the arm after a night at the stone, and the hand after a lifetime of nights (5.5). The born word for one who treats a body.

names.name: Ākās
names.namer: the first comers, through the born
names.why: The first comers were arrivals, and arrivals say the islands are in the sky over the living ground, so they named the islands' common metal for the sky; the born have no word for the islands and say it only as a smith's word out of the patterns, as for the lens bait (1.8, 3.6, 4.8, 6.2).

names.name: Jalit
names.namer: the first comers, through the born
names.why: The ore lies beside the molten rock and is still warm when cut, and the metal comes off the anvil holding that heat and burns what it enters (6.2, 6.7). The first comers named it for that, and the born have the word with the smith's trade.

names.name: Gahan
names.namer: the first comers, through the born
names.why: The lowest rock of the living ground, lying on the wood. Nothing made of the living ground's own matter cuts it (6.2). The first comers named the metal for where it lies and how it yields, and the born have the word with the smith's trade. The old name tied the metal to the moon, which is what the born say of the deep kind and not of the ore.

names.name: Iron
names.why: Ordinary iron, the one hard metal a wood fire melts (6.2). The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Hīrak
names.namer: the first comers, through the born
names.why: The first comers named the clear gem that is cleaved on the anvil's edge and takes a finer edge than iron for the diamond, and smiths still use the name because they hold it is a stone and not crystal, though it is lees set past crystal (6.2, 6.4).

names.name: Tala
names.namer: the first comers, through the born
names.why: The same metal as the inner one, lying lower in the hollow, down to the standing water over the body of the root; the first comers named it for where it lies, and smiths count and sell it as a second metal (6.2).

names.name: Patik
names.namer: the first comers, through the born
names.why: The islands' metal with that world's crystal grown through it, named by the first comers for the crystal that shows in the bar (6.2).

names.name: Stone
names.why: Knapped rubble on a haft, the second tool (6.2). The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Antar
names.namer: the first comers, through the born
names.why: The first metal the first comers cut inside the root, where it lies at every height of the hollow, named for where it lies; the born know it only from bars and from the bait patterns, and call the place itself under (3.4, 3.6, 6.2).

names.name: Wooden

names.name: Coal Ore
names.why: Old timber in the rock (6.3). The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Rubble

names.name: Blue Flower
names.why: One of the two flowers of the islands, spread through the green country; the born cannot know where it came from and the bible names it only by its colour (3.2 bloomvale, 3.5).

names.name: Red Flower
names.why: The bible knows it only as the red flower, the one the first bait uses; the joined name is replaced (3.2 bloomvale, 4.3).

names.name: White Flower
names.why: The other island flower; it has nothing to do with the moon, so the joined name goes (3.2 bloomvale, 3.5).

names.name: Yellow Flower
names.why: A pasture flower with no people's name in the bible; the cute name is replaced by what it is (3.2 plains).

names.name: Stone Furnace
names.why: The block of forge1; an ordinary fire in a ring of rubble (6.4). The present name is already right and stays.

names.name: Stone Furnace
names.why: The burning state of the same block shows the same name (6.4). The present name is already right and stays.

names.name: Gilded Bricks
names.why: Stone faced with gold against the stone-eating kinds, the rim of the burrower's bowl (3.7, 6.3). The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Glass
names.why: Sand set by fire (6.4). The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Fungus Planks
names.why: As the fungus stem (3.4 hollows).

names.name: Fungus Stem
names.meaning: the stem of a great fungus
names.why: The great capped fungi are the hollow's only timber; the joined name is replaced (3.4 hollows).

names.name: Teal Fungus Cap
names.meaning: a teal cap of a great fungus
names.why: As the fungus stem (3.4 hollows).

names.name: Violet Fungus Cap
names.meaning: a violet cap of a great fungus
names.why: As the fungus stem (3.4 hollows).

names.name: Hollow Rock
names.why: The rock that lies between two faces of the wood and rings the third forge (3.4, 6.4). Every other block of the hollow has a plain name, and so has its rock. The old name glued two nouns.

names.name: Glowing Mushroom
names.why: The glowing fungus of the hollow and of the woodland floors; the cute joined name is replaced (3.4, 3.7, 6.9).

names.name: Gold Block
names.why: The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Gold Ore
names.why: Gold lies deep and stays soft (6.3). The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Turf
names.meaning: grass with the soil it grows in
names.why: A piece of grassed soil lifted whole; "block" is a game word and the plain word for the thing is turf, as the bible says of the hollow and the islands (3.1, 3.4, 3.5).

names.name: Gravel
names.why: Floor of the deep sea, with flint in it (3.2 ocean). The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Holder's Bed
names.why: It is a holder's seat for the night, hide over boards because a holder sits up on it every night, and the householder who takes it is no guest, since the hearth under that roof is the householder's (1.6, 5.2, 6.9); holder is the plain word the ground chapter fixes.

names.name: Hollow Gate Frame
names.meaning: the frame of a gate to the hollow
names.why: The frame block of the hollow gate; plain words of the crews who build it (1.6 Gates, 6.4 Gate frames). The present name is already right and stays.

names.name: Hollow Gate
names.why: The opening the remains loosen inside the frame (1.6 Gates). The present name is already right and stays.

names.name: Ice
names.why: Ice is ground and does not count as water (3.1). The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Iron Block
names.why: The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Iron Ore
names.why: Iron of the upper and middle rock (6.2). The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Kapok Leaves
names.why: The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Kapok Log
names.why: The tree of the wet wood, cut thin on the steppe for the sand country's fires (3.2 savanna, jungle). The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Kapok Planks
names.why: The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Lantern
names.why: An ordinary light, sold by the smith (5.5 smith). The present name is already right and stays.

names.name: Lava
names.why: Stone the sand kinds fed on until it runs (3.3). The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Glowing Frond
names.why: One of the growths that light the hollow; the Latin-sounding word goes, and "lit" is avoided because in householders' mouths it means held (1.6 After the last, 3.4).

names.name: Hīrak Block
names.why: A block of the gem named by the tier word: The first comers named the clear gem that is cleaved on the anvil's edge and takes a finer edge than iron for the diamond, and smiths still use the name because they hold it is a stone and not crystal, though it is lees set past crystal (6.2, 6.4).

names.name: Hīrak Ore
names.why: The rock that carries the gem named by the tier word: The first comers named the clear gem that is cleaved on the anvil's edge and takes a finer edge than iron for the diamond, and smiths still use the name because they hold it is a stone and not crystal, though it is lees set past crystal (6.2, 6.4).

names.name: Geode
names.meaning: a hollow stone lined with crystal
names.why: Lees shut in rock sets dense as a geode; "mana" names no matter on this ground, so the plain word stays alone (1.6, 6.3).

names.name: Mossy Stone
names.why: The mossed stone of the woodland killing floors; named to match rubble and the bible's words (3.2 forest, 3.7).

names.name: Mossy Bricks
names.why: The dais at the woodland stones is mossed brick (3.7). The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Mud
names.why: The mire, where lees sets as it does in rock (3.2 swamp). The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Brown Mushroom
names.why: The brown caps of the shade, the mire and the hollow that go into plain stew; the joined name is replaced (3.2 forest, 6.9).

names.name: Red Mushroom
names.why: An ordinary mushroom; the cute joined name is replaced by what it is (6.9).

names.name: Fungal Turf
names.why: The turf of the hollow, which also took in some caverns of the deep rock; no people of the ground has walked it to name it, so it is said plainly (3.3, 3.4, 3.6).

names.name: Black Glass
names.why: Rock that ran beside the molten rock and set again is black glass, as sand runs to black glass under the sand-country fires; the joined name is replaced by what it is (3.2 desert, 3.3, 6.2).

names.name: Tala Ore
names.meaning: the lower part, base, bottom, with English "ore"
names.why: The ore of the metal named by the tier word: The same metal as the inner one, lying lower in the hollow, down to the standing water over the body of the root; the first comers named it for where it lies, and smiths count and sell it as a second metal (6.2).

names.name: Oak Leaves
names.why: The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Oak Log
names.why: The old wood of the green country (3.2 forest). The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Oak Planks
names.why: The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Birch Leaves
names.why: As the birch log (3.2 palewood).

names.name: Birch Log
names.why: The pale-barked tree that is first to seed into given-up pasture is what English calls a birch; the joined name is replaced by the plain one (3.2 palewood).

names.name: Birch Planks
names.why: As the birch log (3.2 palewood).

names.name: Packed Path
names.why: The packed paths from the well to each door (3.7). The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Pine Needles
names.why: The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Pine Log
names.why: The cold wood (3.2 taiga). The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Pine Planks
names.why: The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Ratan Furnace
names.meaning: the furnace built round the remains of Ratan
names.why: The block of forge4. It has the same name.

names.name: Pale Crystal
names.why: The spires of pale crystal on the islands, the oldest lees on the root; the bible says pale crystal (3.5 rift_shards, 6.3).

names.name: Patik Ore
names.why: The ore of the metal named by the tier word: The islands' metal with that world's crystal grown through it, named by the first comers for the crystal that shows in the bar (6.2).

names.name: Reeds
names.why: Where grass meets water, and in the mire for fibre (3.2). The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Island Gate Frame
names.meaning: the frame of a gate to the islands
names.why: The frame block of the gate to the islands; "rift" claimed a tear that is not there (1.3, 1.6 Gates).

names.name: Island Gate
names.why: The opening to the islands inside its frame; named for the place it reaches, which is the islands (1.3).

names.name: Island Rock
names.why: The rock under the turf of the islands, which rings the fourth forge (3.5, 6.4). Every other block of the islands has a plain name, and so has its rock. The old name glued two nouns.

names.name: Kusum Leaves
names.meaning: the leaves and blossom of the tree of Kusum, the flower country
names.why: The blossoming tree grows in one country only, and nobody can say whether it is an island tree or a tree of the living ground (3.2 bloomvale). It has no English name, so the born, who build with it there, say it by the name of its country. Rosewood is a different real timber.

names.name: Kusum Log
names.meaning: a log of the tree of Kusum, the flower country
names.why: The blossoming tree grows in one country only, and nobody can say whether it is an island tree or a tree of the living ground (3.2 bloomvale). It has no English name, so the born, who build with it there, say it by the name of its country. Rosewood is a different real timber.

names.name: Kusum Planks
names.meaning: planks of the tree of Kusum, the flower country
names.why: The blossoming tree grows in one country only, and nobody can say whether it is an island tree or a tree of the living ground (3.2 bloomvale). It has no English name, so the born, who build with it there, say it by the name of its country. Rosewood is a different real timber.

names.name: Line Frame
names.why: The block of the same station; a frame for cutting lines evenly and laying fibre under tension, named in the plain words the trade already uses (6.4, 6.6).

names.name: Sand
names.why: Rock with the firmness eaten out of it by the sand kinds (3.2 desert). The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Sandstone
names.why: Loose ground that lay long enough over the root and set again (3.2 beach). The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Sandstone Bricks
names.why: The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Scoria
names.why: The rock round the molten rock where it stands highest (3.3). The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Island Soil
names.why: As island turf (3.5 rift).

names.name: Island Turf
names.why: The surface of the earlier world as it stood at its last dusk; no people of the ground lives there or has a word for the islands, and the bible says island turf (3.5 rift, 3.6).

names.name: Snow
names.why: Snow lies where it lies and has never been seen to melt (3.1). The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Snowy Turf
names.why: Snow on the grass of the cold country; named to match turf (3.2 tundra).

names.name: Lamp Fungus
names.meaning: a fungus that hangs like a lamp
names.why: The bible calls these the lamps that hang from the roofs, and they are growth, not made lamps; the joined name is replaced by a plain one that says both (3.4).

names.name: Island Leaves
names.why: Its leaves give light, so nothing comes up under it (3.5 rift).

names.name: Island Log
names.meaning: a log of the island tree
names.why: The island tree with lit leaves, which the first comers camped under; the bible says island tree and island timber, and the joined name goes (3.2 bloomvale, 3.5 rift).

names.name: Island Planks
names.why: As the island log (3.5 rift).

names.name: Stone
names.why: The common rock under every soil (6.2). The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Stone Bricks
names.why: The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Glassed Stone
names.why: Stone the flier's throws have loosened and that has set again as glass, on the pad and up the masts; the joined name is replaced by what happened to it (4.7 The floor).

names.name: Tall Grass
names.why: Pasture grass, cut for fibre (3.2 plains). The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Thatch
names.why: Roofing of the plank and thatch villages (3.7). The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Joining Bench
names.meaning: a bench for joining two worked pieces into one
names.why: A piece of the remains of the first great feeder held between two iron bars over a plank top. Two worked pieces laid against the remains go soft enough to be pressed into one (6.4). The plain name says what is done on it.

names.name: Torch
names.why: Light stops feeders coming up; a torch is a torch (1.6 Night, L.11). The present name is already right and stays.

names.name: Antar Ore
names.why: The ore of the metal named by the tier word: The first metal the first comers cut inside the root, where it lies at every height of the hollow, named for where it lies; the born know it only from bars and from the bait patterns, and call the place itself under (3.4, 3.6, 6.2).

names.name: Guhamāt Furnace
names.meaning: the furnace built round the remains of Guhamāt
names.why: The block of forge3. It has the same name.

names.name: Dressed Stone
names.why: The first comers' dressed stone, common stone that has lain dressed ever since and now needs a stone pick; the bible says dressed stone, and the joined name goes (1.6 The old stonework, 2.3, 6.1).

names.name: Water
names.why: The one sheet of water, in which nothing comes up (3.1). The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Water
names.why: A flowing state with no item, sharing the one literal. The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.why: A flowing state with no item, sharing the one literal. The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.
