names.name: Water
names.why: A flowing state with no item, sharing the one literal. The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Workbench
names.why: Four planks fitted square; an ordinary made thing with a plain name (6.4). The present name is already right and stays.

names.name: Ākās Bar
names.why: A bar of the metal named by the tier word: The first comers were arrivals, and arrivals say the islands are in the sky over the living ground, so they named the islands' common metal for the sky; the born have no word for the islands and say it only as a smith's word out of the patterns, as for the lens bait (1.8, 3.6, 4.8, 6.2).

names.name: Ākās Bow
names.why: A bow is an ordinary thing. It is said by the hardness of its make and the plain word, as the picks and the bars are (6.2, 5.7, L.11).

names.name: Ākās Staff
names.meaning: a staff with a seat of Ākās
names.why: A staff throws as hard as its seat is hard, and each is made of the metal whose seat it carries (6.6). It is said by that metal and the plain word.

names.name: Ākās Sword
names.why: A sword of this hardness is an ordinary thing and is said as one: the word for what it is made of and the plain word for the weapon, as the picks and the bars are (6.2, L.11).

names.name: Ākās Totem
names.meaning: a totem with a billet of Ākās
names.why: A totem is two carved bones and a billet of metal, and what forms on it takes its body from the billet (6.6, 7.5). It is said by that metal and the plain word.

names.name: Apple
names.why: Fruit from trees; nothing is tilled (6.9). The present name is already right and stays.

names.name: Arrow
names.why: A flint head on a shaft (6.7). The present name is already right and stays.

names.name: Mūda
names.meaning: a seal, a stamp; a sign, token; a pass
names.why: A piece broken from the glass floor under a fire that has burned kills for generations. Whoever holds a fire gives them to those who march for it, and one shown at any fire is a night inside the light (5.3). The name is their own word for it.

other.name: Fired Token
other.meaning: the plain words of the peoples chapter (5.3)

names.name: Barbed Arrow
names.meaning: an arrow with a barbed head
names.why: Barbed iron, one of the five heads (6.7). The present name is already right and stays.

names.name: Wild Berries
names.why: What grows without being sown; nothing is tilled, so wild is true (1.6 Food). The present name is already right and stays.

names.name: Whistle
names.why: The whistle packed with remains, on which one more small feeder forms; the beastcaller thinks it works by its sound, and nothing binds (6.7, 5.5 beastcaller, 7.5).

names.name: Lees Lump
names.meaning: a lump of lees set in mud
names.why: Lees that lies in mud sets as it does in rock, and the animal that lies in the mire swallows a lump with the mud (3.2 swamp, 7.3). It is no pearl. Lees is the plain word the ground chapter fixes.

names.name: Bone
names.why: What is left in the pot, and what feeders leave (6.3, 7.3). The present name is already right and stays.

names.name: Spring Boots
names.meaning: boots with a spring in them
names.why: Plain good gear, the boots and the anklet worked into one piece (6.7, 6.12 Join).

names.name: Thorned Guard
names.meaning: a guard for the arm set with thorn
names.why: The thorned guard, set with thorn so that what strikes it is cut (6.7). It is said like the plain guard it is made from.

names.name: Cairn Bow
names.meaning: the bow out of the cairn
names.why: One of the four arms of the first comers that lay in the store under the eighth stone and come out of the animal that ate the store (4.10). It is an ordinary arm and is said in plain English, with the born's word for the place, as the key and the gem are.

names.name: Cairn Sword
names.meaning: the sword out of the cairn
names.why: One of the four arms of the first comers that lay in the store under the eighth stone and come out of the animal that ate the store (4.10). It is an ordinary arm and is said in plain English, with the born's word for the place, as the key and the gem are.

names.name: Nihān Remains
names.meaning: the raw remains of Nihān: the trade's plain word for a piece of a great feeder that has not been boiled down, with the name of the animal
names.why: The raw remains of the strongest of the stone-eating kind, the strongest thing any living person has killed on this ground. Boiled down, one of these is one charge (4.10). The old name claimed a light returned (4.13). Remains is the trade's plain word (6.3), and each of the eight is known by the name of the animal it came from.

names.name: Cairn Key
names.why: The present name is already right: the born say the key opens the cairn, and both words are theirs in the game's English (4.10); it is a small housing with a charge nobody drives (4.10), and the tooltip, not the name, must stop saying it opens anything (4.13).

other.name: bait
other.meaning: a small housing with an undriven charge of slivers and shards, which is what the animal eats (4.10)

names.name: Cairn Staff
names.meaning: the staff out of the cairn
names.why: One of the four arms of the first comers that lay in the store under the eighth stone and come out of the animal that ate the store (4.10). It is an ordinary arm and is said in plain English, with the born's word for the place, as the key and the gem are.

names.name: Cairn Lamp
names.meaning: a totem whose head is a lamp from the housing
names.why: One of the four arms of the first comers that lay in the store under the eighth stone and come out of the animal that ate the store (4.10). It is an ordinary arm and is said in plain English, with the born's word for the place, as the key and the gem are. Its head is a lamp from the housing, and the plain word says so (7.5).

names.name: Stone Scale
names.meaning: a scale of the stone-eating kind
names.why: The plates of the stone-eating kind are scale of the stone it has eaten (7.3). The scale worn at the wrist is one of these (6.7). Chitin is the wrong matter.

names.name: Jalit Bar
names.namer: the first comers, through the born
names.why: A bar of the metal named by the tier word. The ore lies beside the molten rock and is still warm when cut, and the metal comes off the anvil holding that heat and burns what it enters (6.2, 6.7). The first comers named it for that, and the born have the word with the smith's trade.

names.name: Jalit Bow
names.why: A bow is an ordinary thing. It is said by the hardness of its make and the plain word, as the picks and the bars are (6.2, 5.7, L.11).

names.name: Jalit Staff
names.meaning: a staff with a seat of Jalit
names.why: A staff throws as hard as its seat is hard, and each is made of the metal whose seat it carries (6.6). It is said by that metal and the plain word.

names.name: Jalit Sword
names.why: A sword of this hardness is an ordinary thing and is said as one: the word for what it is made of and the plain word for the weapon, as the picks and the bars are (6.2, L.11).

names.name: Jalit Totem
names.meaning: a totem with a billet of Jalit
names.why: A totem is two carved bones and a billet of metal, and what forms on it takes its body from the billet (6.6, 7.5). It is said by that metal and the plain word.

names.name: Cloud Bottle
names.meaning: a bottle of the pale stuff
names.why: It holds a wad of the pale stuff that hangs under the islands, let out under the foot as one step of ground in the air (6.7, 3.5). Arrivals take that stuff for cloud, because they hold that the islands are in the sky, and the block has the same word (1.8). It holds no wind.

names.name: Coal
names.why: Old timber in the rock, or timber charred in the fire (6.3). The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Roast Fish
names.why: Plain, matching Roast Meat (6.9).

names.name: Roast Meat
names.why: Fire trebles what meat is worth (6.9). The present name is already right and stays.

names.name: Wrist Scale
names.meaning: a scale worn at the wrist
names.why: A scale of the stone-eating kind worn at the wrist, which loosens rock a little under the pick (6.7).

names.name: Door
names.why: The item that places a door (1.6 Rooms and townsfolk). The present name is already right and stays.

names.name: Knuckle Band
names.meaning: a band worn over the knuckles
names.why: One of the two bands that add to a blow, which belong to the game and have no cause (6.7, 1.9). The plain name says where it is worn and claims nothing. The old name claimed a duel and a sign.

names.name: Gahan Bar
names.namer: the first comers, through the born
names.why: A bar of the metal named by the tier word. The lowest rock of the living ground, lying on the wood. Nothing made of the living ground's own matter cuts it (6.2). The first comers named the metal for where it lies and how it yields, and the born have the word with the smith's trade. The old name tied the metal to the moon, which is what the born say of the deep kind and not of the ore.

names.name: Gahan Bow
names.why: A bow is an ordinary thing. It is said by the hardness of its make and the plain word, as the picks and the bars are (6.2, 5.7, L.11).

names.name: Kuranga Remains
names.meaning: the raw remains of Kuranga: the trade's plain word for a piece of a great feeder that has not been boiled down, with the name of the animal
names.why: A piece of the strongest of the deep kind, which gives its kind's light. In a ring of black glass it is the fifth forge (4.9). The born call it a coal from the last eclipse, which is their belief about the moon. Remains is the trade's plain word (6.3), and each of the eight is known by the name of the animal it came from.

names.name: Kuranga Mask
names.meaning: a mask for Kuranga: the plain English word for what the born take the vessel to be, with the name of the one it is laid for
names.why: The born say it is worn and the animal sees the wearer; it is laid on the stone like every other bait (4.9). What is laid for the one set over a country is an offering, and householders teach how to make each one (5.2).

other.name: bait
other.meaning: what it is: raw remains of the host's lesser animals in a vessel made to reach one animal (1.6, 4.2)

names.name: Kuranga Tine
names.meaning: a tine of Kuranga: plain English for the piece, with the name of the animal it came from
names.why: It is a sliver of its body, which grows outward as its tines do, and the strongest low remains a person can carry (4.9). Eclipse claimed a tie to the moon. Householders who work remains know each piece by holding it and by what it came from (5.5, tinker).

names.name: Gahan Staff
names.meaning: a staff with a seat of Gahan
names.why: A staff throws as hard as its seat is hard, and each is made of the metal whose seat it carries (6.6). It is said by that metal and the plain word.

names.name: Gahan Sword
names.why: A sword of this hardness is an ordinary thing and is said as one: the word for what it is made of and the plain word for the weapon, as the picks and the bars are (6.2, L.11).

names.name: Gahan Totem
names.meaning: a totem with a billet of Gahan
names.why: A totem is two carved bones and a billet of metal, and what forms on it takes its body from the billet (6.6, 7.5). It is said by that metal and the plain word.

names.name: Carved Bone
names.why: A carved bone with raw shade remains bound to it, which a small feeder forms on because the remains are food (6.6); an effigy is a likeness and claimed the carving did the work (8.11), and the beastcaller's own words are carved bone (5.5).

names.name: Jalit Arrow
names.why: The five arrowheads are five hardnesses (6.7). This head comes off the anvil holding the heat of the deep and burns what it enters, and it is said by its metal, as the bar is.

names.name: Ember Dust
names.why: What the cinder wisp leaves, which burns twice as long as coal (6.3, 7.3); plain words for what it is. The present name is already right and stays.

names.name: Feather
names.why: From the bird, an ordinary animal (6.9). The present name is already right and stays.

names.name: Feather Charm
names.meaning: a small worn piece with a feather
names.why: One of the pieces with the pale stuff of the islands in it, which takes the force out of a landing (6.7). The present name stays.

names.name: Plant Fiber
names.why: Tall grass and reeds for fibre (3.2, 6.9). The present name is already right and stays.

names.name: Flint
names.why: Flint in the gravel of the deep sea (3.2 ocean). The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Vaka Tooth
names.why: A tooth of the pale runner of the cold country (7.3). It is said by the name of the animal, which sets it apart from the tooth of the burrower.

names.name: Cloud Emblem
names.meaning: an emblem with the pale stuff in it
names.why: The piece that gives a second step in the air and a soft landing, made with the pale stuff that arrivals take for cloud (6.7, 1.8). It has no wind in it.

names.name: Jelly
names.why: It is the jelly that rots out of fallen growth, in which the Kinva forms and which lies there when it is killed (7.3 gelcap); a plain word, where the old name glued two words together.

names.name: Fungus Broth
names.why: The lit fungus of the hollow eaten as broth, which feeds and eases the arm a little (6.9); "glowcap" glued two words, and the apothecary's broth needs only the plain words.

names.name: Gold Bar
names.why: The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Greater Salve
names.why: The stronger salve made with growth from the hollow (5.5 apothecary, 6.8). The present name is already right and stays.

names.name: Greater Tonic
names.why: The stronger tonic made with growth from the hollow (5.5 apothecary). The present name is already right and stays.

names.name: Locket
names.meaning: a small hinged case worn on a chain
names.why: The locket, a number with no cause (6.7, 1.9); heart adds nothing.

names.name: Vanahar Remains
names.meaning: the raw remains of Vanahar: the trade's plain word for a piece of a great feeder that has not been boiled down, with the name of the animal
names.why: A piece of the body of the strongest of the woodland host that has not been boiled down. It still moves, and it loosens only made things (4.3, 6.3). Remains is the trade's plain word (6.3), and each of the eight is known by the name of the animal it came from.

names.name: Hide
names.why: From the grazer, the rooter and some feeders (6.9). The present name is already right and stays.

names.name: Hide Cap
names.why: Present name is already right: hide is the grazer's and rooter's, cut on the workbench, and cap is the plain word (6.4 workbench, 6.9).

names.name: Hide Vest
names.why: Present name is already right: plain hide work (6.4 workbench, 6.9).

names.name: Hide Trousers
names.why: Present name is already right: plain hide work (6.4 workbench, 6.9).

names.name: Hollow Gate
names.why: A frame of hard matter round remains that hold a relation to the hollow (1.6 Gates); crews build gates and no householder goes through one (5.2), so the crews' plain words name it, and the hollow is the plain word for that place (1.3). The present name is already right and stays.

names.name: Iron Bar
names.why: The present name is the plain word for what it is and stays.

names.name: Iron Bow
names.meaning: a bow of the iron hardness
names.why: A bow is an ordinary thing. It is said by the hardness of its make and the plain word, as the picks and the bars are (6.2, 5.7, L.11).

names.name: Arm Guard
names.meaning: an iron guard for the arm
names.why: Plain good gear: the iron guard for the arm (6.7). The plain name leaves out the metal, so that it is not read as a piece of iron armour.

names.name: Iron Staff
names.meaning: a staff with an iron seat
names.why: A staff throws as hard as its seat is hard, and each is made of the metal whose seat it carries (6.6). It is said by that metal and the plain word.

names.name: Iron Sword
names.why: A sword of this hardness is an ordinary thing and is said as one: the word for what it is made of and the plain word for the weapon, as the picks and the bars are (6.2, L.11).

names.name: Iron Totem
names.meaning: a totem with an iron billet
names.why: A totem is two carved bones and a billet of metal, and what forms on it takes its body from the billet (6.6, 7.5). It is said by that metal and the plain word.

names.name: Bark Draught
names.why: A bark draught that toughens skin for a few minutes, ordinary herb-work (6.9); "ironbark" glued two nouns and claimed iron.

names.name: Worn Coin
names.why: The coin that brings more from a kill belongs to the game and has no cause (6.7, 1.9). The name claims no metal, since coin on this ground is lees by weight (1.6), and it leaves the word lucky to the modifier.

names.name: Hīrak
names.why: The gem itself, cleaved and never smelted: The first comers named the clear gem that is cleaved on the anvil's edge and takes a finer edge than iron for the diamond, and smiths still use the name because they hold it is a stone and not crystal, though it is lees set past crystal (6.2, 6.4).

names.name: Hīrak Bow
names.why: A bow is an ordinary thing. It is said by the hardness of its make and the plain word, as the picks and the bars are (6.2, 5.7, L.11).

names.name: Hīrak Staff
names.meaning: a staff with a seat of Hīrak
names.why: A staff throws as hard as its seat is hard, and each is made of the metal whose seat it carries (6.6). It is said by that metal and the plain word.

names.name: Hīrak Sword
names.why: A sword of this hardness is an ordinary thing and is said as one: the word for what it is made of and the plain word for the weapon, as the picks and the bars are (6.2, L.11).

names.name: Hīrak Totem
names.meaning: a totem with a billet of Hīrak
names.why: A totem is two carved bones and a billet of metal, and what forms on it takes its body from the billet (6.6, 7.5). It is said by that metal and the plain word.

names.name: Shell
names.why: Lodeshell is two nouns glued; the shell that draws loose things in is a number with no cause (6.7, 1.9).

names.name: Crystal Charm
names.why: Crystal-work that eases a driving arm; mana claims stored power, and the blue bar is the arm's strain (6.7, 6.6, 8.11).

names.name: Crystal
names.why: Lees set hard; "mana" names nothing on this ground, and the plain word is what every crew says (1.6, 6.6).

names.name: Eyeglass
names.meaning: a lens of ground glass for the eye
names.why: Plain good gear: the ground glass that helps an archer's eye (6.7).

names.name: Maruhar Tooth
names.meaning: a tooth of Maruhar: plain English for the piece, with the name of the animal it came from
names.why: It is a tooth, the one part of the animal harder than its plates (4.4). Householders who work remains know each piece by holding it and by what it came from (5.5, tinker).

names.name: Moon Sliver
names.why: Everyone says the things of the dark night come down from the moon and that their slivers are pieces of it (1.8, 7.3 moonspawn); the name carries that false belief, as names here do. The present name is already right and stays.

names.name: Vanahar Sprig
names.meaning: a sprig of Vanahar: plain English for the piece, with the name of the animal it came from
names.why: It is a shoot off the body that still puts out leaf (4.3); Mossheart was two evocative nouns glued. Householders who work remains know each piece by holding it and by what it came from (5.5, tinker).

names.name: Moth Dust
names.why: The flier of the hollow is bodied in the dust that falls from the great caps and leaves it (7.3 umbral_moth). The present name is already right and stays.

names.name: Guhamāt Cap
names.meaning: a cap of Guhamāt: plain English for the piece, with the name of the animal it came from
names.why: It is a piece of the cap, on which low feeders form as they formed on the pieces that fell from the animal (4.6). Householders who work remains know each piece by holding it and by what it came from (5.5, tinker).

names.name: Tala Bar
names.meaning: the lower part, base, bottom, with English "bar"
names.why: A bar of the metal named by the tier word: The same metal as the inner one, lying lower in the hollow, down to the standing water over the body of the root; the first comers named it for where it lies, and smiths count and sell it as a second metal (6.2).

names.name: Tala Bow
names.why: A bow is an ordinary thing. It is said by the hardness of its make and the plain word, as the picks and the bars are (6.2, 5.7, L.11).

names.name: Tala Staff
names.meaning: a staff with a seat of Tala
names.why: A staff throws as hard as its seat is hard, and each is made of the metal whose seat it carries (6.6). It is said by that metal and the plain word.

names.name: Tala Sword
names.why: A sword of this hardness is an ordinary thing and is said as one: the word for what it is made of and the plain word for the weapon, as the picks and the bars are (6.2, L.11).

names.name: Tala Totem
names.meaning: a totem with a billet of Tala
names.why: A totem is two carved bones and a billet of metal, and what forms on it takes its body from the billet (6.6, 7.5). It is said by that metal and the plain word.

names.name: Patik Arrow
names.why: The five arrowheads are five hardnesses (6.7). This one is headed with the islands' metal that has crystal through it and is said by its metal, as the bar is.

names.name: Patik Bar
names.why: A bar of the metal named by the tier word: The islands' metal with that world's crystal grown through it, named by the first comers for the crystal that shows in the bar (6.2).

names.name: Patik Bow
names.why: A bow is an ordinary thing. It is said by the hardness of its make and the plain word, as the picks and the bars are (6.2, 5.7, L.11).

names.name: Ratan Crystal
names.meaning: a crystal of Ratan: plain English for the piece, with the name of the animal it came from
names.why: It is a piece of the densest crystal there is (4.8). Householders who work remains know each piece by holding it and by what it came from (5.5, tinker).

names.name: Ratan Remains
names.meaning: the raw remains of Ratan: the trade's plain word for a piece of a great feeder that has not been boiled down, with the name of the animal
names.why: A piece of the strongest of the islands' crystal kinds. In a ring of the rock of the islands it is the fourth forge (4.8). Remains is the trade's plain word (6.3), and each of the eight is known by the name of the animal it came from.

names.name: Ratan Lens
names.meaning: a lens for Ratan: the plain English word for what the born take the vessel to be, with the name of the one it is laid for
names.why: The born say the lens gathers light and the light calls the animal, their account of a bait that works by the shards it holds flat (4.8). What is laid for the one set over a country is an offering, and householders teach how to make each one (5.2).

other.name: bait
other.meaning: what it is: raw remains of the host's lesser animals in a vessel made to reach one animal (1.6, 4.2)

names.name: Patik Staff
names.meaning: a staff with a seat of Patik
names.why: A staff throws as hard as its seat is hard, and each is made of the metal whose seat it carries (6.6). It is said by that metal and the plain word.

names.name: Patik Sword
names.why: A sword of this hardness is an ordinary thing and is said as one: the word for what it is made of and the plain word for the weapon, as the picks and the bars are (6.2, L.11).

names.name: Patik Totem
names.meaning: a totem with a billet of Patik
names.why: A totem is two carved bones and a billet of metal, and what forms on it takes its body from the billet (6.6, 7.5). It is said by that metal and the plain word.

names.name: Guhamāt Remains
names.meaning: the raw remains of Guhamāt: the trade's plain word for a piece of a great feeder that has not been boiled down, with the name of the animal
names.why: A piece of the strongest of the hollow's fungus kinds. In a ring of the rock of the hollow it is the third forge (4.6). A great feeder is an animal and has no queen (4.13). Remains is the trade's plain word (6.3), and each of the eight is known by the name of the animal it came from.

names.name: Raw Fish
names.why: The fish as food is plain fish; the creature has its own name, and food takes the plain word (6.9).

names.name: Raw Meat
names.why: Meat of the ordinary animals (6.9). The present name is already right and stays.

names.name: Long Glove
names.why: The long glove that adds reach (6.7); Longarm is two words glued.

names.name: Recall Stone
names.meaning: a stone that takes its bearer back
names.why: Crystal and cut lines round a gem, the same crossing as a fall made on purpose, taking the bearer back to the bed (1.6); arrivals find and use it, and the plain words say what it does. The present name is already right and stays.

names.name: Island Gate
names.why: There is no rift: the far place is the islands, what is left of the root's own world (1.3), and the crews who build the kit name it in plain words for where it opens (1.6 Gates).

names.name: Vihanga Scale
names.why: A scale of the broad flier of the islands (7.3), said by the name of the animal. The old name used a word for the place that is gone.

names.name: Rust Lump
names.why: The rustbound is bodied in the rust of the harness it ate and has no bone in it (1.6, 7.3 rustbound); "core" is the ward word for root-wood under a housing (1.2) and must not be used of anything else.

names.name: Crystal Ring
names.why: Crystal-work, crystal on a short line worn where the driving arm can use it; there are no sages and no spells (6.7, 6.6).

names.name: Healing Salve
names.why: Fruit, mushroom and fibre bound on a wound, ordinary herb-work (6.9). The present name is already right and stays.

names.name: Maruhar Remains
names.meaning: the raw remains of Maruhar: the trade's plain word for a piece of a great feeder that has not been boiled down, with the name of the animal
names.why: A piece of the burrower's middle, which is bodied in rock from beside the molten rock. In a ring of deep rock it is the second forge (4.4). Householders say it is hot enough to melt the ore, which is false: the remains loosen the ore, and no fire does. Core is the ward word for root-wood (1.2), so the old word goes. Remains is the trade's plain word (6.3), and each of the eight is known by the name of the animal it came from.

names.name: Shade Flesh
names.why: It is the shade-kind's own matter raw, the body of bone and dark matter it took from other feeders (7.3 gloomshade); "essence" claimed a spirit, and the plain words say what is cut from the body.

names.name: Dark Cloak
names.why: The dark cloak, woven with the stuff of the shade-kind, hard to see at its edges (6.7); gloam is a poetic word.

names.name: Shard
names.why: The Sakal is splintered crystal and leaves a shard (7.3 shardling); "living" claimed a life the crystal does not have.

names.name: Island Fruit
names.why: The fruit that hung on the island trees at that world's last dusk, brought back by crews (6.9); "sky" glued an evocative noun on and stated the arrivals' mistake that the islands are overhead (1.8) as fact in every mouth, including the provisioner's, who sells it.

names.name: Cloud Treads
names.meaning: treads with the pale stuff under the heel
names.why: Boots with the pale stuff under the foot and the heel (6.7). They are said with the word arrivals use for that stuff, which sets them apart from the plain boots.

names.name: Crystal Pendant
names.why: The larger crystal piece that does what the ring and the charm do; soul and reliquary are temple words, and 8.11 asks for it renamed (6.7, 8.11).

names.name: Cairn Gem
names.why: It is a piece of housing with its gem in it, and householders take the housing for the cairn they say closed their chief stone (4.10); sovereign and light claim a rule and a lighting that the kill never gives (4.13).

names.name: Guhamāt Smoker
names.meaning: a smoker for Guhamāt: the plain English word for what the born take the vessel to be, with the name of the one it is laid for
names.why: It smoulders the sacs on the fungus so that the smoke carries in the still air of the hollow (4.6). The plain word for a pot that makes smoke is used, since a censer is a temple vessel. What is laid for the one set over a country is an offering, and householders teach how to make each one (5.2).

other.name: bait
other.meaning: what it is: raw remains of the host's lesser animals in a vessel made to reach one animal (1.6, 4.2)

names.name: Spore Sac
names.why: What a Kavak leaves; three make the bait for the hollow's fungus strongest (7.3 sporeling). The present name is already right and stays.

names.name: Anklet
names.meaning: a band worn round the ankle
names.why: Plain good gear: the anklet that helps the legs (6.7); spring adds nothing the effect line does not say.

names.name: Mushroom Stew
names.why: The brown caps make a plain stew (6.9); a plain name that does not depend on the cap's own name.

names.name: Stick
names.why: Ordinary timber (6.2). The present name is already right and stays.

names.name: Stone Bow
names.meaning: the bow made at the stone hardness
names.why: The bow a crew makes once it is knapping stone, the second of the ten hardnesses (6.2). It is said like the stone sword beside it. The old name glued two nouns.

names.name: Stone Sword
names.why: A sword of this hardness is an ordinary thing and is said as one: the word for what it is made of and the plain word for the weapon, as the picks and the bars are (6.2, L.11).

names.name: Jīmūt Kite
names.meaning: a kite for Jīmūt: the plain English word for what the born take the vessel to be, with the name of the one it is laid for
names.why: It is a kite, flown from the stone to put the bait in the air (4.7). What is laid for the one set over a country is an offering, and householders teach how to make each one (5.2).

other.name: bait
other.meaning: what it is: raw remains of the host's lesser animals in a vessel made to reach one animal (1.6, 4.2)

names.name: Jīmūt Remains
names.meaning: the raw remains of Jīmūt: the trade's plain word for a piece of a great feeder that has not been boiled down, with the name of the animal
names.why: A piece of the pale stuff the flier is bodied in. It stands up from the hand however it is held, and six bars round one of these are the second gate (4.7). Remains is the trade's plain word (6.3), and each of the eight is known by the name of the animal it came from.

names.name: Walking Boots
names.why: Plain good gear, leather cut to fit a body: the boots that help the legs (6.7). Strider is a cute coinage.

names.name: Maruhar Lure
names.meaning: a lure for Maruhar: the plain English word for what the born take the vessel to be, with the name of the one it is laid for
names.why: The born speak of calling it up; a burrower is reached by a lure sunk through the loose sand, which the gold weighs down (1.6, 4.4). What is laid for the one set over a country is an offering, and householders teach how to make each one (5.2).

other.name: bait
other.meaning: what it is: raw remains of the host's lesser animals in a vessel made to reach one animal (1.6, 4.2)

names.name: Flower Tea
names.why: It is a flower tea that quickens the legs (6.9); the old name glued two words and called a flower a root.

names.name: Jīmūt Feather
names.meaning: a feather of Jīmūt: plain English for the piece, with the name of the animal it came from
names.why: It is the same pale stuff as the plume, bears weight and has almost none (4.7); tempest carried the storm the born speak of. Householders who work remains know each piece by holding it and by what it came from (5.5, tinker).

names.name: Thorn
names.why: Thorn is what the Kantak is bodied in and leaves (1.6, 7.3); the plain word, shortened.

names.name: Fins
names.why: The fins are plain good gear; tide adds nothing, and nothing flows on this ground (6.7, invented.md: water).

names.name: Tonic
names.why: Ground crystal in fruit juice, the drink a holder takes at first light (5.5 apothecary, 6.6); there is no mana (8.11).

names.name: Antar Bar
names.why: A bar of the metal named by the tier word: The first metal the first comers cut inside the root, where it lies at every height of the hollow, named for where it lies; the born know it only from bars and from the bait patterns, and call the place itself under (3.4, 3.6, 6.2).

names.name: Antar Bow
names.why: A bow is an ordinary thing. It is said by the hardness of its make and the plain word, as the picks and the bars are (6.2, 5.7, L.11).

names.name: Antar Staff
names.meaning: a staff with a seat of Antar
names.why: A staff throws as hard as its seat is hard, and each is made of the metal whose seat it carries (6.6). It is said by that metal and the plain word.

names.name: Antar Sword
names.why: A sword of this hardness is an ordinary thing and is said as one: the word for what it is made of and the plain word for the weapon, as the picks and the bars are (6.2, L.11).

names.name: Antar Totem
names.meaning: a totem with a billet of Antar
names.why: A totem is two carved bones and a billet of metal, and what forms on it takes its body from the billet (6.6, 7.5). It is said by that metal and the plain word.

names.name: Vanahar Likeness
names.meaning: a likeness for Vanahar: the plain English word for what the born take the vessel to be, with the name of the one it is laid for
names.why: Householders say the log must be carved as a likeness and they put a red flower on it; the remains in it do the work (4.3). What is laid for the one set over a country is an offering, and householders teach how to make each one (5.2).

other.name: bait
other.meaning: what it is: raw remains of the host's lesser animals in a vessel made to reach one animal (1.6, 4.2)

names.name: Antar Arrow
names.why: The five arrowheads are five hardnesses (6.7). This one is headed with the metal of the hollow and is said by its metal, as the bar is. The old name claimed a shade.

names.name: Kankāl Bell
names.meaning: a bell for Kankāl: the plain English word for what the born take the vessel to be, with the name of the one it is laid for
names.why: The born ring the iron cup set mouth down on the stone and call it a bell; the sound does nothing (4.5). What is laid for the one set over a country is an offering, and householders teach how to make each one (5.2).

other.name: bait
other.meaning: what it is: raw remains of the host's lesser animals in a vessel made to reach one animal (1.6, 4.2)

names.name: Kankāl Remains
names.meaning: the raw remains of Kankāl: the trade's plain word for a piece of a great feeder that has not been boiled down, with the name of the animal
names.why: A piece of the strongest of the shade-kind. Seven pieces of black glass round one of these are the first gate (4.5). The old name made it a sign and the animal a warden. Remains is the trade's plain word (6.3), and each of the eight is known by the name of the animal it came from.

names.name: Kankāl Plate
names.meaning: a plate of Kankāl: plain English for the piece, with the name of the animal it came from
names.why: It is a plate of the pale set matter of its body (4.5); warden and aegis claim a guard. Householders who work remains know each piece by holding it and by what it came from (5.5, tinker).

names.name: Arm Ring
names.meaning: a ring worn on the arm
names.why: One of the two bands that add to a blow, a number with no cause (6.7, 1.9); warrior is an office word for a person and the plain piece is a ring on the arm.

names.name: Crystal Fiber
names.why: It is fibre laid round crystal, the same path as a cut line made up as cloth (6.4); there are no spells (8.11), so it takes the plain words for what it is.

names.name: Wooden Bow
names.why: A bow is an ordinary thing. It is said by the hardness of its make and the plain word, as the picks and the bars are (6.2, 5.7, L.11).

names.name: Wooden Sword
names.why: A sword of this hardness is an ordinary thing and is said as one: the word for what it is made of and the plain word for the weapon, as the picks and the bars are (6.2, L.11).

names.name: Anvil
names.why: A block of iron heavy enough to stand under a hammer; ordinary smithing (6.4). The present name is already right and stays.

names.name: Chest
names.why: A box; ordinary goods in it draw nothing (6.4). The present name is already right and stays.

names.name: Stone Furnace
names.why: A wood or coal fire in a ring of rubble that melts the soft ores; an ordinary fire with a plain name (1.6 Fire, 6.4). The present name is already right and stays.

names.name: Maruhar Furnace
names.meaning: the furnace built round the remains of Maruhar
names.why: The born carry the pattern of the four forges built round great remains (2.3), and each is known by the animal whose remains lie in its bed. This one is a piece of Maruhar in a ring of the deep rock it passed through, with a fire under it (6.4). Furnace is the plain word, as for the stone one. The old name glued two nouns.

names.name: Guhamāt Furnace
names.meaning: the furnace built round the remains of Guhamāt
names.why: The born carry the pattern of the four forges built round great remains (2.3), and each is known by the animal whose remains lie in its bed. This one is a piece of Guhamāt in a ring of the rock of the hollow, with a fire under it (6.4). Furnace is the plain word, as for the stone one. The old name glued two nouns.

names.name: Ratan Furnace
names.meaning: the furnace built round the remains of Ratan
names.why: The born carry the pattern of the four forges built round great remains (2.3), and each is known by the animal whose remains lie in its bed. This one is a piece of Ratan in a ring of the rock of the islands, with a fire under it (6.4). Furnace is the plain word, as for the stone one. The old name glued two nouns.

names.name: Kuranga Furnace
names.meaning: the furnace built round the remains of Kuranga
names.why: The born carry the pattern of the four forges built round great remains (2.3), and each is known by the animal whose remains lie in its bed. This one is a piece of Kuranga in a ring of black glass, with a fire under it (6.4). Furnace is the plain word, as for the stone one. The old name glued two nouns.

names.name: Hand
names.why: Making by hand is splitting, knapping, tying and mixing, ordinary work (6.4). The present name is already right and stays.

names.name: Line Frame
names.why: Nothing on this ground carries runes or words (2.3, L.11) and the thing is no loom; it is the crews' frame that holds a stave true while lines are cut along it and lays fibre under even tension, so it takes the plain words of the trade, line and frame (6.4).

names.name: Joining Bench
names.meaning: a bench for joining two worked pieces into one
names.why: A piece of the remains of the first great feeder held between two iron bars over a plank top. Two worked pieces laid against the remains go soft enough to be pressed into one (6.4). The plain name says what is done on it.

names.name: Workbench
names.why: A true flat face and a vice, ordinary carpentry that every cutter knows (1.6 Making, 6.4). The present name is already right and stays.

names.name: True
names.why: Arcane claims secret power; the fact is that its grain runs one way from hand to head so a line cut along it leaks less, and true is the word the bible uses of lines and edges that lie right (6.10, 6.12, 5.5 runescribe).

names.name: Favoured
names.why: Blessed names a god; it set all at once with no soft place, smiths cannot do it on purpose, and the born call it favour, so the name carries their word (6.10).

names.name: Brittle
names.why: Present name is already the plain word for the fact: hammered after it set, with cracks too fine to see (6.10).

names.name: Dull
names.why: Present name is already the plain word for the fact: the edge never closed (6.10).

names.name: Fleet
names.why: The present name stays: the bible gives this label no cause and it belongs to the game (6.10, 1.9).

names.name: Heavy
names.why: Present name is already the plain word for the fact: it set dense, more metal than its size (6.10).

names.name: Keen
names.why: Present name is already the plain word for the fact: the edge closed to a single line with no flaw (6.10).

names.name: Lucky
names.why: The present name stays: the bible gives this label no cause and it belongs to the game (6.10, 1.9).

names.name: Flecked
names.meaning: marked with small spots of something
names.why: Menacing is a mood; the fact is a grain of a strong kill's lees set in the piece (6.10).

names.name: Glowing
names.why: Old lees has set into the metal and it shows a faint cold light; glowing says that without praise (6.10, 6.2 eclipse).

names.name: Quenched
names.why: Savage is a mood; the fact is that the metal passed through a feeder or was quenched in lees, and loosens a little where it cuts (6.10).

names.name: Dense
names.why: Stalwart is a word for a person; the fact is that it set dense throughout, turns more and weighs more (6.10).

names.name: Lean
names.meaning: having little substance for its size
names.why: The fact is that it set with less metal in it than its shape suggests; lean says that, and light would be read as lamplight (6.10).

names.name: Vital
names.why: The present name stays: the bible gives this label no cause and it belongs to the game (6.10, 1.9).

names.name: Thick
names.why: Warding takes the word ward for a plate; the fact is that it set thickest where blows land (6.10, 1.2 Wards).

names.name: Surface
names.why: A crew's plain word for where the matter lay: surface matter and green work, timber, rubble, hide, fibre (6.10). Common is a loot-table word.

names.name: Upper
names.why: Matter of the upper rock, worked by fire: iron (6.10, 6.2 iron).

names.name: Deep
names.why: Matter of the deep rock of the living ground: the gem and cinder (6.10, 6.2).

names.name: Hollow
names.why: Matter from between two faces of the wood, which is the hollow (6.10). The grade is said by the plain word for the place.

names.name: Island
names.why: Matter of the earlier world, which is the islands (6.10). The grade is said by the plain word for the place.

names.name: Floor
names.why: Matter that lay on the wood itself; arrivals call the root's face the floor and take it for stone (6.10, 1.3, 1.8).

names.name: Old
names.why: A made thing that has lain made since the first comers; relic is a word for the holy dead and a loot-table word, and old is the plain fact (6.10, 4.10).

names.name: Rested
names.why: A body that slept a night through mends faster for a short time (6.9). The present name is already right and stays.

names.name: Well Fed
names.why: A full meal leaves a body mending faster for a while (6.9). The present name is already right and stays.

names.name: Toughened
names.why: The status from the bark draught, which toughens the skin (6.9); plain, like Well Fed and Rested.

names.name: Quickened
names.why: The status from the flower tea, which quickens the legs (6.9).

names.name: Sand March
names.meaning: a march of the sand-country people
names.why: They are people on a march from a fire, not a host, which is a feeders' word (5.3, 8.11); the householders whose houses it reaches say plainly who comes.

other.name: Payāna
other.meaning: setting out, a march: the sand-country people's own word for what they do (5.3)

names.name: Amāvassa
names.why: The moon is wholly dark on the eighth night of its round, which is the only calendar (1.3). The born have a word for that night, and since the strongest of the shade-kind was killed it is the night the deep kind comes up (1.6). A banner that says the born's word states nothing false, where the old name stated their belief about the moon as fact (8.11).

other.name: the hollow moon
other.meaning: the born's belief, said in English: they say the moon is hollow that night and that what was in it has come down (1.6, 1.8). It belongs in a born mouth

other.name: the dark night
other.meaning: the ground chapter's plain words

names.name: Night raid
names.why: The broken woodland host goes for stores at dusk; the string says nothing false (1.6, 8.11). The present name is already right and stays.

names.old: The ground remembers how to stand up.
names.name: Roots come up through the paving.
names.meaning: plain English, said of what a hunter on the floor sees
names.why: When it comes up at a stone its roots go into the joints of the paving and up the oaks (4.3); the line says what a hunter sees, not that the ground does anything (4.13).

names.old: Roots tear free of the altar.
names.name: Its roots tear up out of the paving.
names.meaning: plain English, said of what a hunter on the floor sees
names.why: At half strength it pulls itself off the floor it has rooted into (4.3).
Dropped: the bar shows the name alone. The name already carries the householders' belief, a line under it would gloss it (L.2), and 4.13 replaces every title, which the old one was.

names.name: Hoofbeats come up out of the dark.
names.meaning: plain English, said of what a hunter on the floor sees
names.why: It runs on four legs and comes up at night under any moon; it does not put the moon out (4.9, 4.13).

names.old: Its antlers catch a light that is not there.
names.name: Its tines light up violet.
names.meaning: plain English, said of what a hunter on the floor sees
names.why: The light on its antlers is the violet light its own kind gives (4.9, 4.13).

names.old: The Hart will not be led back.
names.name: It charges, and is somewhere else.
names.meaning: plain English, said of what a hunter on the floor sees
names.why: At 25% it charges and changes place; nobody leads it (4.9, 4.13).
Dropped: the bar shows the name alone. The name already carries the householders' belief, a line under it would gloss it (L.2), and 4.13 replaces every title, which the old one was.

names.name: Crystal gathers over the stone and turns.
names.meaning: plain English, said of what a hunter on the floor sees
names.why: It hangs with a ring of pieces of its own crystal body turning round it (4.8); light is not what it is (4.13).

names.name: The crystals round it begin to turn.
names.meaning: plain English, said of what a hunter on the floor sees
names.why: The ring round it is pieces of its own body (4.8); light edit only (4.13).

names.old: It burns too bright to hold its shape.
names.name: It stops holding its shape, and pieces come away.
names.meaning: plain English, said of what a hunter on the floor sees
names.why: At 25% it stops holding its body and pieces come away, on which its lesser kind form (4.8).
Dropped: the bar shows the name alone. The name already carries the householders' belief, a line under it would gloss it (L.2), and 4.13 replaces every title, which the old one was.

names.name: The sand in the bowl begins to move.
names.meaning: plain English, said of what a hunter on the floor sees
names.why: It comes up from below through the loose sand carried into the bowl (4.4); the sand is not breathing (4.13).

names.old: The Maw thrashes, shedding grit and fury.
names.name: It stays up and thrashes, shedding grit.
names.meaning: plain English, said of what a hunter on the floor sees
names.why: At 45% it stays up and thrashes, and the grit it sheds draws its lesser kind (4.4); fury and the old name go (4.13).
Dropped: the bar shows the name alone. The name already carries the householders' belief, a line under it would gloss it (L.2), and 4.13 replaces every title, which the old one was.

names.old: The sky leans down to look at you.
names.name: Something large circles over the kite.
names.meaning: plain English, said of what a hunter on the floor sees
names.why: The kite puts the bait in the air, the only place it feeds, and it circles and does not land (4.7, 4.13).

names.name: Pieces of it begin to fall on the floor.
names.meaning: plain English, said of what a hunter on the floor sees
names.why: The strikes on marked ground fall from it because it is overhead; there is no thunder (4.7, 4.13).

names.old: The Regent screams, and the storm answers.
names.name: It screams and stoops lower.
names.meaning: plain English, said of what a hunter on the floor sees
names.why: The stoop is how it takes anything; storm is the born's word for it overhead and nothing answers (4.7, 4.13).
Dropped: the bar shows the name alone. The name already carries the householders' belief, a line under it would gloss it (L.2), and 4.13 replaces every title, which the old one was.

names.old: It was here before the light. It kept it.
names.name: Stone moves inside the cairn.
names.meaning: plain English, said of what a hunter on the floor sees
names.why: It lies in the base under the eighth stone and comes up through it to take the bait (4.10); it holds no light for anyone, and the line drops the banned word (README 13).

names.old: Stone grinds on stone. The cairn opens its eye.
names.name: Stone grinds on stone. The stack parts, and its lit middle shows.
names.meaning: plain English, said of what a hunter on the floor sees
names.why: At 66% the stack parts and its lit middle shows, which the born call an eye (4.10); the eye goes (4.13).

names.old: All the light it ever kept, all at once.
names.name: It is coming apart, and everything in it shows.
names.meaning: plain English, said of what a hunter on the floor sees
names.why: At 33% it is coming apart and everything in it shows at once (4.10). It held nothing for anyone, so the line says what a hunter on the floor sees.
Dropped: the bar shows the name alone. The name already carries the householders' belief, a line under it would gloss it (L.2), and 4.13 replaces every title, which the old one was.

names.name: The smoke reaches the roof, and the roof moves.
names.meaning: plain English, said of what a hunter on the floor sees
names.why: The censer's smoke carries in the still air, and the dome over the floor is the growth the animal hangs by (4.6, 4.13).

names.name: Its cap splits, and the inside glows.
names.meaning: plain English, said of what a hunter on the floor sees
names.why: At 55% the wound opens the cap and the inside gives the light all fungus gives there (4.6); light edit only (4.13).

names.old: Sporemother tears loose from her roots!
names.name: Its growth tears from the roof, and it swings.
names.meaning: plain English, said of what a hunter on the floor sees
names.why: At 20% most of the growth that held it tears and it swings on what is left (4.6).
Dropped: the bar shows the name alone. The name already carries the householders' belief, a line under it would gloss it (L.2), and 4.13 replaces every title, which the old one was.

names.old: A bell tolls with no bell to toll it.
names.name: The bell is rung, and something pale comes up.
names.meaning: plain English, said of what a hunter on the floor sees
names.why: The born ring the cup that holds the bait, and that can be said; the animal is pale with the deep kind it ate (4.5, 4.13).

names.name: It turns, throwing pale matter in spirals.
names.meaning: plain English, said of what a hunter on the floor sees
names.why: What the game called raising both hands is the animal turning to throw in spirals; it has no hands (4.5, 4.13).

names.old: The seal cracks. So does the Warden.
names.name: It is coming apart, and the smaller ones come for it.
names.meaning: plain English, said of what a hunter on the floor sees
names.why: At 25% it begins to fail to hold its body and the shade-kind come in for it; nothing was sealed (4.5, 4.13).
Dropped: the bar shows the name alone. The name already carries the householders' belief, a line under it would gloss it (L.2), and 4.13 replaces every title, which the old one was.

names.name: Steel Saw
names.why: A two-handled saw of steel from another world, made by cutters for broken root-wood; steel is a metal nobody makes on this ground, and plain words say what a crew sees (6.11).

names.name: Wire Net
names.why: A throwing net of island wire with weighted rim, from a store on the islands, for which the born have no word at all (6.11, 3.6).

names.old: a sealed jar of great lees
names.name: Sealed Jar
names.why: A first comers' clay jar of salted great lees; to the householders it is lees in a jar, the plain thing every hearth wants, and nobody living has seen one opened (6.11, 1.6 Coin).

names.name: Ward Core
names.why: A core cut on another world, set under an old hearthstone by first comers who built house wards the way they are built elsewhere; core is the fixed plain word (6.11, 1.2 Wards).

names.old: a harness made for a born hunter
names.name: Heavy Harness
names.why: Gem scale over cinder plate, heavier than anything an arrival wears; householders deny that the born ever hunted, so nobody on the ground calls it a hunter's, and a crew calls it by what it is (6.11, 1.5, 2.4).

names.old: a crystal in the shape of a pot
names.name: Crystal Jar
names.meaning: crystal in the shape of a jar
names.why: A single crystal with the form of the inside of a jar whose clay broke off it; plain words say what it is, and it is where a player sees that crystal is lees (6.11).

names.old: a bench with stronger remains in it
names.name: Sealed Bench
names.why: A bench built round the remains of the hollow's strongest, sealed in a room of a dungeon; the tinker has never seen one, and a crew names it for how it is found (6.11, 6.12, 5.5 tinker).

names.name: Stone Staff
names.why: A first comers' rod of dressed stone with cut lines and a gem seat, from before anyone here cut lines in wood; it lies in a vault in the hollow, where no born person goes, so it has only the crew's plain name (6.11, 3.6).
